title: Reserved strokes
goal: What is pinned before any word is placed, and why no word takes a punctuation, command or letter stroke.

blocks.x: Every command, punctuation mark and fingerspelled letter in a keymux config for lyk is pinned **before any word is placed**, ahead of briefs. No word can take a stroke such as [[TP-BG]] (`!`).

head: File in `rules/reserved/`
Deployed as
Holds
Where it is listed
rows: 87 strokes: the silent `#` that opens the [name lane](#/ref/names), cursor, editing, shortcuts, case and spacing commands, F-keys, engine control (suspend, toggle, unload), overlay and lookup controls, undo and history helpers (including `{:back}`)

130 strokes: 78 marks and symbols (12 of them the `#` [wrap strokes](#/ref/punctuation/wrapping-a-word-in-a-pair-of-marks)), and the 52 glued fingerspelling letters (first-up, `*` exempt: `{:firstup:except=*}`)
1,470 modifier chords: Ctrl/Alt/Super/Shift plus a letter, digit, symbol or key, all first-up with the right-hand base exempt (`{:firstup:except=-FRPBLGTS}`)

items: Nothing generated competes with a reserved stroke: not a word's plain outline, not a brief, not a star form, not an alternate pronunciation, not a phrase, not a backup.

A word that wanted a reserved stroke moves to its next-cheapest outline. Examples: [[captain|KAPT]] would have been `K*P` (the glued capital K), and [[eh|A*EU]] would have been `*E` (the glued letter e).
A reserved stroke goes back to words only by removing it from the reserved file. [[up|-P]] and [[am|-PL]] sit on `-P` and `-PL` because the period has its one stroke, [[TP-PL]].

**One stroke per output.** No two outlines in these three files type the same thing: every mark, command and modifier chord has one stroke, the one struck most in the typed tape, else the fewest keys. `cargo test` asserts it (`every_reserved_output_has_exactly_one_outline`). The strokes this freed (alternate periods, commas, question marks, and thousands of modifier chords differing only by a key the dictionary ignores) belong to words and phrases.

blocks.x: The build refuses to run if a brief named `[word]` in `rules/briefs.toml` has a reserved literal outline.
The lists themselves are on the next pages: [punctuation and commands](#/ref/punctuation), [fingerspelling, numbers and modifiers](#/ref/fingerspelling).
